feature.name: health-badge
feature.description: Source-agnostic health badge (HealthWidget, formerly StepsWidget) in OneBarWidget — today's steps, optional heart rate, and the producing source_id. Google Fit is one source (OAuth2 offline access, helper script apps/desk/scripts/google-fit-auth.cjs, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN in apps/desk/.env, optional GOOGLE_FIT_STEPS_SOURCE); the LAN push inlet POST /display/health is another. A Google-Fit-only view carries a "Google Fit ends late 2026" tooltip. See ADR 012 and E021-T02/T03/T04.
feature.transports: Desktop reads over Tauri IPC with a 5-min success interval and a 1/2/5/10/30-min backoff ladder; the remote display reads `health` out of the RemoteDisplayState WS snapshot and never polls (src/hooks/useHealth.ts owns both).
feature.error-model: Backend classifies failures as auth_revoked (invalid_grant / 401 → re-run OAuth helper) or transient (network / 5xx / parse → exponential backoff)

feature.name: remote-write-gate
feature.description: The remote server's read routes stay open on the LAN; every route that WRITES app state passes remote_auth::require_token — a constant-time compare against DESK_REMOTE_TOKEN. An unset token answers 503 (closed), a wrong one 401, so "unconfigured" can never be mistaken for "working". Bodies are capped before parsing (1 KiB health, 4 KiB voice) and an unusable value answers 422, so a malformed push never looks like an empty one. See ADR 020 and E021-T03.
feature.routes: GET /display/ws and GET /display/api open; POST /display/health and POST /display/voice authenticated

feature.name: voice-dictation
feature.description: Phone-only dictation panel on /display posting to POST /display/voice. Keyboard-mic dictation into a textarea is the primary path; the browser's SpeechRecognition button is progressive enhancement, shown only when the API exists and the mic permission is not denied (E021-D5 — /display is plain HTTP, which Chrome will not give a secure context). voice_intent::parse maps the transcript offline to Intent (Snooze/Note/WalkStart/WalkEnd) over PL+EN regexes; unrecognised text is always a Note. The pipeline writes events, never engine state: EventLogger VOICE line → voice_notes row → side effect → optional BYOK AI reply → desk:voice-ack broadcast → webhook push. Snooze is the ONLY intent with a side effect and it sets CommunicationPolicy's existing snooze fields; nothing here touches session_*.rs (E021-D3 / ADR 015). Every leg is independently optional. See ADR 021 and E021-T05/T06/T08.
feature.events: desk:voice-ack (WS DisplayEvent, wire name pinned against desk_events::DESK_VOICE_ACK by test)
feature.storage: voice_notes table in SQLite + a VOICE line in logs/YYYY-MM-DD/events.log; discoverable in Analyst → Catalog

feature.name: phone-notifications
feature.description: Optional outbound push so replies reach the user away from the desk: notify_webhook::WebhookNotifier posts {title, message, priority, tags} to an ntfy-shaped endpoint for the sit-limit alert and every voice acknowledgement. Android shows it as a phone notification and mirrors it to a paired watch — the watch runs no MoveUp code (E021-D1 / ADR 021). Fire-and-forget: spawned on tokio, never awaited, 5s per attempt, one retry on 5xx/timeout, none on 4xx. Gated by AppConfig.notify_webhook_enabled (default off); URL from AppConfig.notify_webhook_url else DESK_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL. See E021-T07.

layer.name: relay-worker
layer.note: Standalone pnpm project (own pnpm-workspace.yaml, own lockfile) deployed to Cloudflare Workers — NOT a member of the app workspace. Imports the wire contract from the app through the `@app/*` alias so the protocol schema exists once. E022-T02 ships the room and the router; credentials/REST are T03, command routing is T04, so the Worker is not yet deployable.
layer.file: Router: GET /healthz (version, for the deploy gate), /app/* (viewer build via the ASSETS binding; 503 assets_unavailable when ../dist has not been built, never 404), GET /v1/desks/:deskId/ws (upgrade forwarded to the DeskRoom named by desk_id — the token is never a URL component), and the six REST credential routes as 501 stubs

DeskRoom Durable Object on the WebSocket Hibernation API: hello→welcome, one desk + N viewers, event fan-out, desk_status on arrival/departure, ping/pong, and a single alarm sweeping both the hello deadline (4401) and the idle deadline (1001). Holds the newest snapshot in memory only — it dies with the object, which is what lets the relay store nothing about a person's day

Envelope building plus readFrame(), which turns a parse failure into a decision: close 4400 for an unparseable/wrong-version/non-envelope frame, a non-fatal error frame carrying the offending id for a bad payload or an unknown type
Per-socket state in the socket's attachment (survives hibernation) rather than in accept-time tags (fixed before the role is known, and taggable only by leaking the role into the upgrade URL)

verifyToken — the seam T03 fills with a D1 lookup; today a shape check that already rejects with 4401, plus hashToken and a constant-time hex compare. Refuses outright once a DB is bound but unread, so a half-wired deployment cannot accept any well-formed string as a credential
Entitlement lookup skeleton and the fixed REST error-code list; findLicense distinguishes "no such license" (null) from "could not ask" (throws)
responses.ts (one {error:{code,message}} shape), health.ts, assets.ts, rest.ts (the route table + a :param matcher; wrong verb on a real path answers 405, not 404)
licenses / desks / viewers — SHA-256 hashes and metadata only. Read and written by T03
Mints a key and prints its hash; exits 3 until T03 stores it, because a key nobody stored entitles nobody
